answer: Eclipse-Distance Admission requires each new identity to connect only through a distinct set of relay neighbors that are themselves mutually non-adjacent, a juniper-like sparse cut in the peer graph. An identity whose neighborhood overlaps an existing cluster's is throttled until it acquires links from separate regions. Forging a Sybil cohort therefore costs a full set of fresh, non-overlapping relays per identity, scaling linearly with each fake node at dawn of admission. Honest singletons pay one neighborhood; attackers pay a comet's tail of disjoint infrastructure.
